spec.functions: dav1d_load_tmvs_rvv(const refmvs_frame *rf, int tile_row_idx, int col_start8, int col_end8, int row_start8, int row_end8)
spec.formula: load_tmvs_c in context/reference_refmvs.c: for every 8x8 block row in [row_start8, row_end8) and column in [col_start8, col_end8): read the candidate projection from rf->rp_ref[rf->mfmv_ref[n]] rows, scale each temporal MV by the per-(n,ref) distances rf->mfmv_ref2cur / rf->mfmv_ref2ref (the C's exact fixed-point scale with rounding and clipping to the MV range), write the projected MV and the reference index into rf->rp_proj; blocks whose candidate is invalid get ref = -1 / the C's INVALID_MV handling
spec.domain: 1 <= n_mfmvs <= 7; tile column ranges up to the frame width in 8x8 blocks (checkasm: iw8 = 240, ih8 = 63, row window of 16); rp_stride = 240; every VLEN 128..1024; RVV 1.0 + Zba/Zbb
width_bounds: MV scaling is the C's exact fixed-point arithmetic (sign, rounding, clip): reproduce it bit-exactly, including the INVALID_MV sentinel
rp_proj is written only in [row_start8, row_end8) x [col_start8, col_end8); rp_ref rows are read-only
refmvs_temporal_block and the projection layout are packed structs: mind the element widths and stride in bytes

regimes.bench: checkasm --bench: full row window, all n_mfmvs references valid (mfmv_ref2cur/ref2ref = 1), one cell: load_tmvs
regimes.check: checkasm: random tile column ranges, 3 references, random ref distances, invalid candidates present

candidates.application: strip-mine the block columns with vsetvli; the column tail is a smaller vl
candidates.expected_gain: no scalar epilogue over the row

candidates.title: Per-(n, ref) scale factors staged in scalar registers or a small in-register table
candidates.application: mfmv_ref2cur[n] and mfmv_ref2ref[n][r] are per-call constants; hoisting them out of the column loop (and folding the sign flips) removes per-block table loads
candidates.expected_gain: inner loop reads only the projection buffers

candidates.title: Bit-exact temporal scaling in e32
candidates.application: the fixed-point MV scale (multiply by the distance ratio with the C's rounding and clipping) maps to vmul/vsmul plus vmin/vmax at e32, widening only where the C's precision requires
candidates.expected_gain: vectorizes the arithmetic core without changing any rounding
preconditions: INVALID_MV must map to the C's output, not a scaled value

candidates.title: Write rp_proj MV+ref as packed 8-byte units
candidates.application: the projection entry packs the 32-bit MV and the reference index: assemble both in one register group and store once per block instead of two
preconditions: the packed layout matches the struct, byte for byte

candidates.application: row strips at the largest LMUL the register budget allows; the per-block work is independent across columns
